about: Concept graph of the AI engineering track: what each concept needs first (requires; python:<id> is a concept of the Python track), what it lets you do (can), its lesson and its exercises.

concepts.name: The AI engineering stack and planning an application
concepts.can: Can describe the three layers of the AI stack (application, model, infrastructure), how AI engineering differs from ML engineering and from full-stack work, and how to judge a use case before building (value, risk, evaluation, maintenance)

concepts.name: How LLMs are built
concepts.can: Can explain in plain words what pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and preference tuning do, what a transformer's attention does at a glance, and why model size and test-time compute change quality and cost

concepts.name: What a token is
concepts.can: Can explain tokens, why limits, cost and speed are counted in them, and estimate the tokens of a text roughly

concepts.name: Calling a chat model API
concepts.can: Can make a chat completion request (roles, messages, parameters) to any provider's API or SDK, and read the answer, the finish reason and the token usage

concepts.name: Context windows and context rot
concepts.can: Can explain what is in the context window, why a model is stateless, what happens when input does not fit, and why long prompts are followed less reliably

concepts.name: Sampling and determinism
concepts.can: Can say what temperature, top-p and max tokens do, and when to use temperature 0 and why it is still not a guarantee

concepts.name: Cost and latency arithmetic
concepts.can: Can estimate the cost and latency of a workload from tokens in and out and per-million-token prices

concepts.name: API errors, rate limits and retries
concepts.can: Can tell retryable errors (rate limit, timeout, overload) from permanent ones and retry with exponential backoff and a cap

concepts.name: Structuring a prompt
concepts.can: Can separate instructions, context, input and output format in a prompt, use delimiters, and say why a vague prompt gives unstable output

concepts.name: Few-shot examples
concepts.can: Can add well-chosen examples to a prompt, keep them out of the evaluation set, and say when examples help less than a clearer instruction

concepts.name: Structured output and validation
concepts.can: Can get JSON from a model reliably (schemas, validation, retry on invalid output) and say why to parse, never string-match

concepts.name: Validating model output with a schema
concepts.can: Can validate a model's output against a schema (for example with Pydantic or JSON Schema), turn failures into a specific retry message, and reject what cannot be repaired

concepts.name: Hallucination and grounding
concepts.can: Can explain why models state false things confidently, and name three mitigations (grounding in supplied text, citations, abstaining) with their limits

concepts.name: Reasoning prompts and test-time compute
concepts.can: Can explain chain-of-thought prompting and reasoning models, what extra thinking tokens buy and cost, and when a plain answer is better

concepts.name: Multimodal inputs and outputs
concepts.can: Can send an image or audio to a model through an API, generate an image or speech, and name the limits (cost, resolution, errors on small text)

concepts.name: What an embedding is
concepts.can: Can explain an embedding as numbers whose distance means similarity, and cosine similarity in words

concepts.name: Similarity search with embeddings
concepts.can: Can embed texts through an embedding API or local model, compute cosine similarity and return the top k matches for a query

concepts.name: Chunking
concepts.can: Can split documents into chunks (by structure, size and overlap), and explain how chunk size changes retrieval quality and cost

concepts.name: Keyword search and BM25
concepts.can: Can explain an inverted index and BM25, and say when keyword search beats vectors (exact codes, names, rare terms)

concepts.name: Vector databases and indexes
concepts.can: Can say what a vector database adds over a list (approximate nearest-neighbour indexes, filtering, persistence) and when pgvector or an in-memory index is enough

concepts.name: Hybrid search and reranking
concepts.can: Can combine keyword and vector results (for example reciprocal rank fusion) and explain what a reranker adds and costs

concepts.name: Ingestion pipelines
concepts.can: Can load, clean, deduplicate and chunk documents, attach metadata for filtering, and re-index only what changed

concepts.name: The RAG pipeline
concepts.can: Can build and explain a retrieve-then-generate pipeline: chunk, embed, store, retrieve, assemble the prompt, generate, and cite

concepts.name: Citations and grounded answers
concepts.can: Can make a RAG answer cite the passages it used, and abstain when the retrieved text does not contain the answer

concepts.name: Debugging RAG
concepts.can: Can tell a retrieval failure (the right passage was not found) from a generation failure (found but misused), and find which with a labelled set

concepts.name: RAG versus long context versus tools
concepts.can: Can argue when to use RAG, a long context window or agentic retrieval with tools, on cost, freshness, accuracy and security

concepts.name: Tool (function) calling
concepts.can: Can describe a function to a model, handle the model's request to call it, run it in code and return the result, in a loop that ends

concepts.name: Workflows versus agents
concepts.can: Can say whether a task needs a fixed workflow or an agent, and name the common workflow patterns (chaining, routing, parallelisation, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimiser)

concepts.name: The agent loop
concepts.can: Can write and explain an agent loop with a step limit, stop conditions and error handling, and say how a runaway agent is stopped

concepts.name: Designing tools for agents
concepts.can: Can design a tool with a clear name, description, small typed arguments and useful errors, and say what makes a tool easy for a model to misuse

concepts.name: The Model Context Protocol
concepts.can: Can explain MCP (hosts, clients, servers; tools, resources, prompts), the problem it solves, and when a plain function or CLI is simpler

concepts.name: Context engineering and memory
concepts.can: Can decide what goes into an agent's context each turn (instructions, tool results, memory, retrieved facts) and how to keep it small

concepts.name: Agent frameworks and when to skip them
concepts.can: Can compare plain API calls with an agent framework (for example LangGraph or a vendor agent SDK) on control, debugging, lock-in and what the framework gives

concepts.name: Multi-agent systems
concepts.can: Can say when several agents (orchestrator and workers, hand-offs, debate) beat one, what they cost in tokens and complexity, and how they share state

concepts.name: Agentic RAG
concepts.can: Can turn a fixed retrieve-then-generate pipeline into an agent that decides when and what to search (search as a tool, several queries, stop when enough), and say when the fixed pipeline is better

concepts.name: Planning and reflection in agents
concepts.can: Can explain planning (decomposing a goal into steps), ReAct-style reasoning between actions and reflection on results, and where plans go wrong (drift, loops, over-planning)

concepts.name: Why evaluate
concepts.can: Can explain why a few good-looking examples is not an evaluation, and what a test set, a metric and a baseline are

concepts.name: Error analysis
concepts.can: Can read a sample of real outputs, label what went wrong, group the failures and rank them, before building any metric

concepts.name: Building a golden set
concepts.can: Can build a labelled test set from real inputs, keep it separate from prompt examples, and grow it from production failures

concepts.name: Graders: code checks and LLM judges
concepts.can: Can choose between a code check and an LLM judge, write a judge rubric, and check a judge against human labels

concepts.name: Regression evals in CI
concepts.can: Can run an evaluation set automatically on every prompt or model change and fail the build below a threshold

concepts.name: Evaluating RAG and agents
concepts.can: Can evaluate retrieval and generation separately for RAG, and an agent's trajectory and outcome, not only its final answer

concepts.name: Judging a new model release
concepts.can: Can decide whether to switch to a new model by running your own evaluation set, cost and latency, instead of a public benchmark

concepts.name: The model landscape and choosing a model
concepts.can: Can compare model families and sizes (closed and open-weight, general and small), read a model card, and shortlist models for a task by capability, cost, latency, licence and context length

concepts.name: Local versus hosted models
concepts.can: Can argue when to use a hosted API, a self-hosted open-weight model or a hybrid, on quality, data control, cost and operations

concepts.name: Quantisation and local inference
concepts.can: Can explain quantisation and what it trades, estimate the memory a model needs, and run a small model locally (for example with Ollama or llama.cpp)

concepts.name: Fine-tune or not
concepts.can: Can say when prompting, RAG or fine-tuning is the right tool (style and format against knowledge), and what fine-tuning costs to do and to keep

concepts.name: Preparing fine-tuning data
concepts.can: Can build, clean and split a fine-tuning dataset, keep the test set apart, and check for leakage and bias

concepts.name: LoRA and parameter-efficient fine-tuning
concepts.can: Can explain LoRA and why it needs far less memory than full fine-tuning, and run or read a small LoRA fine-tune with a library such as Hugging Face PEFT

concepts.name: Dataset engineering and synthetic data
concepts.can: Can curate, deduplicate and augment a dataset, generate synthetic examples with a model, and check them for errors, bias and leakage before training or evaluation

concepts.name: Serving a model behind an API
concepts.can: Can wrap a model call in a web service (for example FastAPI) with validation, streaming responses and clear error codes

concepts.name: Secrets, configuration and access control
concepts.can: Can keep API keys out of code and images, load them from the environment or a secret store, and give a service the least cloud permissions it needs

concepts.name: Containers for AI services
concepts.can: Can package a model-calling service in a Docker image, with pinned dependencies, and explain what changes when a GPU is needed

concepts.name: Managed model services in the cloud
concepts.can: Can compare calling a provider directly with a cloud's managed service (for example Amazon Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex AI): models offered, regions, quotas, identity, billing and data terms

concepts.name: Serving open models on GPUs
concepts.can: Can explain what an inference server such as vLLM does (batching, KV cache), size a GPU for a model, and choose between an endpoint and self-hosting

concepts.name: Scaling and cloud cost
concepts.can: Can reason about autoscaling, serverless against dedicated capacity, quotas, spot instances and budgets, and set a spending alert before experimenting

concepts.name: Inference optimisation
concepts.can: Can explain the main levers for faster, cheaper inference (quantisation, KV cache, continuous batching, speculative decoding, smaller or distilled models) and their trade-offs

concepts.name: Reliability: timeouts, fallbacks and budgets
concepts.can: Can set timeouts, retries, fallbacks to another model and token or cost budgets, and say what happens when the main model is slow, overloaded or retired

concepts.name: Caching: prompt, response and semantic
concepts.can: Can explain prompt caching (reused prefixes), exact response caching and semantic caching, and what silently breaks a cache

concepts.name: Reducing latency
concepts.can: Can name and order the levers for latency (streaming, shorter prompts and outputs, smaller models, parallel calls, caching)

concepts.name: Observability for LLM features
concepts.can: Can say what to trace and log for an LLM call (inputs, model, parameters, tokens, latency, cost, prompt version, outcome) and what not to log (secrets, personal data)

concepts.name: Cost control and routing
concepts.can: Can reduce cost per completed task (cheaper model for easy cases, caching, shorter prompts, batching) and measure that quality held

concepts.name: Architecture of a production AI application
concepts.can: Can draw the parts around a model in production (gateway, router, guardrails, retrieval, cache, queue, logging) and say what each protects against

concepts.name: User feedback and UX for AI
concepts.can: Can design feedback collection (explicit ratings, edits, implicit signals), turn it into evaluation cases, and design an interface that shows uncertainty and lets users correct the system

concepts.name: Orchestrating pipelines
concepts.can: Can schedule ingestion, re-indexing and evaluation runs with an orchestrator or a simple scheduler, with retries, alerts and run history

concepts.name: Prompt injection
concepts.can: Can explain direct and indirect prompt injection with an example of each, and say why a model refusing is not a control

concepts.name: Excessive agency and least privilege
concepts.can: Can limit what an agent can do (scoped tools, read-only by default, human approval for irreversible actions) and explain why

concepts.name: Guardrails and output validation
concepts.can: Can validate inputs and outputs in code (allow-lists, schemas, length, moderation) and place the checks outside the model

concepts.name: Sensitive data and model routing
concepts.can: Can decide which data may go to a hosted model, which must be redacted or kept local, and what to ask a provider about retention and training use

concepts.name: MCP and tool security
concepts.can: Can name the risks of installing a third-party tool server (tool poisoning, over-broad permissions, data exposure) and the controls

concepts.name: Regulation basics
concepts.can: Can summarise what the EU AI Act asks of a team that ships a chatbot (transparency, risk classes) and where to check the current text

concepts.name: Responsible AI: bias, fairness and moderation
concepts.can: Can name where bias enters a system (data, model, prompt, use), test for it with paired inputs, use content-moderation tools, and run simple adversarial tests
